QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_27

question.text: Regarding side-letters with AIF investors, SEBI regulations broadly:

answer.text: Require SEBI approval for each side-letter individually
Impose restrictions on what additional rights can be granted via side-letters
Require all side-letters to be publicly disclosed on SEBI website

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (page 235), side-letters are used to document specific arrangements with individual investors, and there are restrictions within SEBI regulations on what additional rights can be granted via a side-letter. The manager owes a fiduciary duty to all investors and must operate within the SEBI-defined restrictions on side-letter terms. The Trap: Outright prohibition overstates the position - side-letters are permitted, subject to restrictions. Per-side-letter SEBI approval and mandatory public disclosure on the SEBI website are fictional procedures. Note: Side-letters must respect the manager's fiduciary duty and the SEBI restrictions on additional rights. Careful drafting and clear documentation help avoid challenges from investors who are not party to the side-letter.
